title: First 30 Days: Access Orchestration & Cognitive Load Checklist
content:
Goal: create a pragmatic, low-friction 30-day onboarding checklist that combines access orchestration (so new hires can actually do meaningful work day 1-30) with lightweight cognitive-load checks so managers can pace ramping without burning people out. This doc is an operational playbook + interview-rubric snapshot used by hiring managers and people-ops to: 1) reduce day-0 friction; 2) make interview signals actionable in ramp; 3) track cognitive load and task density for the first month.

High-level principles (keep short, share with hiring manager in offer thread):
- Minimum Viable Access (MVA) first: grant the smallest set of permissions that enable the first three practical tasks for the role. Avoid broad entitlements by default.
- Evidence continuity: map 3 interview evidence points to 3 onboarding tasks (e.g., debugging a failing test = task: reproduce + write first fix PR).
- Cognitive pacing: intentionally stagger task complexity across week 1-week 4 based on interview signals (seniority markers + self-reported past experience).
- Async-first documentation: ensure every step references a single source-of-truth Confluence page; link to tickets for any manual steps.

Hiring-plan snippet (for managers to paste into req/offer):
- Role orientation: 90% technical onboarding, 10% culture/rituals first 2 weeks.
- Interview-to-ramp mapping: each candidate scorecard maps to a 30-day task list. Use rubric tags: system-design, infra-debug, user-facing-bug, communication.
- Offer language addendum (sample line): "We will provide staged access for the first 30 days and pair you with a designated shadow buddy to align tasks to interview evidence."

Interview rubric (compact version we use to translate signals into ramp expectations):
- Category: Problem solving (score 1-5). Signal: independent debugging, decomposition. Ramp implication: assign 1 mid-size bug to own by end of week 2.
- Category: System knowledge (1-5). Signal: prior infra experience, familiarity with distributed tracing. Ramp implication: scheduled deep-dive with SRE in week 2.
- Category: Communication & async (1-5). Signal: clear PR descriptions + triage decisions. Ramp implication: owner of one async doc update in week 3.
- Category: Learning agility (1-5). Signal: tries new tools quickly, asks good probing questions. Ramp implication: auto-enroll in 1 microlearning module and paired review session.

Day 0 checklist (MUST be done before first standup):
- HR: signed offer, benefits onboarding email sent.
- IT inventory: laptop imaged with baseline image (include list of preinstalled tools: VSCode, chrome, 1password, slack, zoom).
- Accounts provisioned: Okta + SSO, GitHub (repo access request submitted), GCP/Azure project viewer, internal Confluence read. If any access is delayed, create a limited-time shared sandbox and schedule follow-up.
- Calendar: 30/60/90 blocks pre-booked with manager and buddy; 30-min sync with People Ops.
- Intro doc: prefilled welcome doc shared to new hire with team rituals, expectations, and checklist link.

Week 1 (focus = orientation + low-friction wins):
- Day 1-2 tasks (low risk): run test suite locally, reproduce a small bug, submit a tiny docs PR.
- Shadow pairing: 2x 90-minute sessions with buddy doing walkthroughs of codebase and infra runbooks.
- Cognitive-load check: end-of-week 1 15-minute async pulse (quick form): "Did you feel overloaded this week? Which tasks felt unclear?" Manager should review replies and reschedule complexity if >1 overloaded flag.
- Manager to schedule 1:1 expectation-setting and set 3 measurable outcomes for week 2.

Week 2 (focus = ownership of a small deliverable):
- Task: own a non-blocking bug or small feature (est 1-3 days). Deliverable: PR with tests + clear description.
- Infra onboarding: guided session with SRE on staging deploys and observability dashboard.
- Cognitive-load checkpoint: manager-run 20-minute sync focused on pacing and psychological safety; note if hire asks for more clarity or slowed cadence.

Week 3 (focus = cross-team context + async contribution):
- Assign: own a cross-repo doc update or runbook improvement (translates communication rubric to ramp).
- Introduce to product/PM for context deep-dive.
- Microlearning: complete 1 short course (15-30 minutes) chosen from curated list: codebase navigation, infra tracing, security basics.

Week 4 (focus = measurable contributor + feedback loop):
- Deliverable: ship small feature or complete cyclical bug + deploy to staging.
- Feedback: 30-minute formal feedback touchpoint using simple template (three things: did well, one improvement, unblock requests).
- 30-day review: pass/fail signals. Pass if: 1) delivered at least 2 evidence-linked tasks; 2) shows safe ability to triage; 3) manager confirms cognitive load is manageable. If fail, create a 30->60 remediation plan.

Access orchestration matrix (quick reference; manager completes at offer):
- Level 1 (MVA): Git read, Confluence read, issue tracker comment, staging viewer.
- Level 2: PR create on non-critical repos, staging deploy trigger, logs access.
- Level 3 (after manager approval): production deploy, elevated infra entitlements.

Shadow pairing protocol (to reduce onboarding tax on team):
- Buddy selection: prefer same subteam and same time zone. If not possible, select cross-zone buddy with overlapping 3-hour window.
- Session template (90 mins): 1) 15-min orientation; 2) 45-min screen-sharing walkthrough of 1 focused task; 3) 30-min hands-on pairing where new hire drives while buddy blocks.
- Responsibility matrix: buddy handles context for first 14 days; manager remains decision owner. Buddy should log 3 wins the hire achieved and 3 remaining gaps at day 14.

Cognitive load operationalization (simple, repeatable):
- Signal buckets: green (comfortable), yellow (slightly overloaded), red (overloaded).
- Data sources: weekly pulse form (3 quick q's), manager observation notes in hiring doc, number of open blockers assigned to new hire.
- Escalation: any red -> immediate workload reduction (pull one major task), reassign buddy deep dive, and call People Ops if red persists >1 week.

Practical templates (pasteable snippets):
- PR description standard: "What I changed / Why / How I tested / Backwards compat notes / Related interview evidence (tag: system-design/infra/comm)"
- Manager note to hiring panel (pre-offer): "Candidate scored 4 on problem solving and 2 on infra familiarity; plan: pair with SRE and assign infra-focused task week 2."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we auto-provision sandbox repos for hires when GitHub approval lags? Pros: reduces day-0 friction. Cons: security and cleanup overhead. Need legal signoff. (JIRA: HR-731).
- What’s the minimum set of KMS access for staging debugging? Tag SRE on Confluence page: /security/kms-staging.
- Consider building a small onboarding micro-quiz (5 Qs) that maps to rubric signals; low priority.

Appendix: quick links
- Confluence onboarding canonical: confluence:ONBOARD-1184
- Onboarding pulse form (internal): https://forms.internal/onboard-pulse
- People Ops handbook: confluence:PEOPLE-ops/ops-handbook

Quick log (example usage):
- 2026-01-12: updated cognitive-load escalation flow after SRE sync.
- 2025-11-05: initial draft circulated to hiring managers; got feedback about shadow time length.

If using this doc: copy into candidate offer packet and into manager pre-1st-week checklist. Keep it concise in the offer thread and link back to this living doc for details.

Notes: this file is intentionally pragmatic — not a policy. For policy-level entitlements or exceptions, route to security-and-compliance team and reference the policy id.

---

End of doc. "
